full_judgment:
7. Being aggrieved by the order dated 6.2.85 the petitioner filed Writ Petition No. 22 of 1985 challenging the said order dated 6.2.85. The order dated 6.2.85 is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure B. The Writ Petition No. 22 of 1985 was heard by this court and the Rule was discharged by the judgment and order dated 13.7.86 on the ground that the petitioner's ACR for 3 preceding years was not available and as such his case could not be considered by the selection committee. The petitioner preferred a Civil Misc. Petition No. 43 of 1986 before the Appellate Division against the said judgment and order of this court in Writ Petition No. 22 of 1985. While the said Civil Misc. Petition was pending before the Appellate Division the order No. WE/TA-12/85-230 dated 6.8.86 was issued by the Deputy Secretary, Government of Bangladesh, Port Shipping and IWT rescinding and cancelling the impugned order No. 68 of 1985 dated 6.2.85. Since the said letter dated 6.8.86 gave the relief sought by the petitioner, the petitioner preferred a petition before the Appellate Division praying for withdrawal of the said Misc. Petition No. 43 of 1986 and the Appellate Division was pleased to dismiss the said application for non-prosecution. The order dated 6.8.86 passed by the Deputy Secretary cancelling the order No. 68/85 dated 6.2.85 is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure 'C'. It is claimed by the petitioner that in view of the order dated 6.8.86 (Annexure C) the promotion of the respondent Nos. 5-8 in terms of office order dated 68/85 dated 6.2.85 (Annexure B) was cancelled and the Authority as directed by the concerned Ministry was required to fill up the said 4 posts of Senior Deputy Directors by constituting the selection committee and that the case of the petitioner was to be considered on the basis of ACR for 1983-1985 together with other eligible candidates. It is submitted by the petitioner that having regard to the said order dated 6.8.86(Annexure C) the respondent No. 1 was under a legal obligation to finalize the selection through the selection committee. It is further submitted that the order dated 6.8.86 was operative and as it created a vested legal right in the petitioner, he did not proceed with the Civil Misc. Petition No. 43 of 1986. But in spite of the vested right in violation of the Ministry's directive, the impugned order dated 17.12.86 was issued by Mr. Dihider A. Sobhan, Assistant Secretary (Establishment) BIWTA reviving and making operative the order No. 68/85 dated 6.2.85 in respect of the promotion of the respondent Nos. 5 to 8 to the posts of Senior Deputy Directors. The result was that the order dated 6.2.85 (Annexure B) was revived and the order dated 6.8.86 (Annexure C) issued by the Government was made 'nugatory' by the Authority to the prejudice of the petitioner. By a further order No. 31/88 dated 10.1.88 issued by the Secretary, BIWTA, the respondent Nos. 5 to 8 were promoted as Senior Deputy Directors. It is the order of revival of the previous order of promotion and the order of promotion (Annexures 'B' and 'H') which have been impugned and the present Rule obtained. 

 "It appears that the Government had considered this letter of BIWTA according to law and the BIWTA had also considered the matter and found that no preceding two years ACR is existing in favour of the petitioner to be considered by the Selection Board for promotion to the post which is to be filled up. It cannot be read in Regulation No. 6 an expression to the effect that 2 years ACR would also mean 4 months ACR or one year and 4 months ACR. Further, the word "preceeding" would mean immediate past two years and shall not include the year during which promotion matter is considered and further in the promotion matter would have been postponed by the Department to show an undue favour, the petitioner to the prejudice of others even then he would not have to his credit actual two years ACR meaning 24 months actual service till August 1985. In the fact above we do not find that the respondent Authority had acted in violation of any law or malafide in not considering petitioner's case for promotion this time." 

 12. Although the petitioner filed Civil Misc. Petition Case No. 43 of 1986 before the Appellate Division it was dismissed for non-prosecution. So the decision of this court in respect of the eligibility as decided in Writ Petition No. 22 of 1985 is final. Considering the new situation arising out of the Ministry's letter dated 6.8.86 Annexure 'C' need to look into the rules which has been annexed by the petitioner to his affidavit-in-reply on which he relies for his contention that the Ministry being the controlling authority the BIWTA is bound by its decision and direction. Annexure 'D' is a notification of the Rules published in the Dhaka Gazette by the then Government of East Pakistan Home (Transport) Department dated 7.1.60. This notification was published in exercise of the powers conferred by section 25 of the East Pakistan Inland Water Transport Authority Ordinance, 1958 (Ordinance No. LXXV of 1958), and in supersession of the notification No. 882-HT, dated the 1st February, 1959 whereby the Government was pleased to make the rules. It was called the East Pakistan Inland Water Transport Authority Rules 1959. The relevant Rule for the instant case is provided in Rule 5 of Chapter IV relating to staff which reads thus: 

 (3) An appeal against any order of the Chairman shall lie with the Authority whose decision shall be final, provided where punishment is imposed by the Authority itself an appeal shall lie with the Government whose decision shall be binding on the Authority." 

 13. Although the petitioner has relied on these rules we find from these rules that the Authority, that is BITWA, has absolute power in respect of promotion and transfer of the petitioner under clause (a) of sub-rule 2. Sub-rule 3 on which the petitioner relies does not provide for any appeal to the Ministry concerning promotion. The proviso to the sub-rule clearly states that appeal to the Government shall only lie where punishment is imposed by the Authority, The instant case being a case of promotion we are of the opinion that the direction of the Government as contained in Annexures 'C' and 'E' of the petition were not binding on the BIWTA. There is nothing to show that the BIWTA had at any stage rescinded its earlier order No. 68/85 dated 6.2.85 promoting the respondent Nos. 5-8 as Senior Deputy Directors. The decision of the Authority in respect of promotion of its officers being final under the rules we find that the order dated 7.12.86 (Annexure 'D') making its earlier order of promotion No. 68/85 dated 6.2.85 operative, to have been made legally and with lawful authority. Consequently we hold that order dated 10.1.88 (Annexure 'H') to have been also made with lawful authority, In the circumstances this Rule directed against Annexures 'D' and 'H' cannot be sustained. 

 18. The case of the petitioner is as follows: He was appointed the Deputy Director, Ports and Traffic, service which has been stated in his earlier writ petitions. He has stated that he was victimized and dismissed by order dated 15.4.89 during pendency of Writ Petition No. 54 of 1988 filed against the Authority's order No. 68/85 dated 6.2.85 promoting his juniors and without considering his case. It is stated that in the said Writ Petition No. 54 of 1988 the stay which was granted on 15.2.88 was vacated on 14.11.88 as the Advocate for the petitioner due to personal difficulties could not appear in the court. Subsequently, the petitioner was transferred to the Authority's Barisal office and the petitioner had to comply with the order and reported for duty at Barisal office on 7.1.89 where he worked till 15.1.89. He fell seriously ill on 16.1.89. The Authority's doctor considering the serious nature of the disease by his certificate dated 15.1.89 advised the petitioner complete rest and immediate admission in Government Hospital. Prior to his departure for Barisal the petitioner was under treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital from 16.11.88 to 28.11.88 and in support of his illness and treatment he has annexed Annexures B4, B5 and B6. Because of his illness he could not draw his salary for the months of November and December, 1988 and he had to rush to Barisal without 2 (two) months arrear salary. With no money to pay his medical expenses, he filed an application at the directive of Authority's doctor, seeking medical leave for treatment at Dhaka Government Officers Hospital stating, inter alia, that he may be permitted to leave the station vide Memo No. 01 dated 15.1.89 Barisal Head Office marked as Annexure 'C' along with the medical certificate marked as Annexure 'D'. Thereafter he came to Dhaka and obtained "no objection certificate" from the Ministry of Shipping to take admission in the hospital for treatment which is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure 'E'. After getting clearance from the Ministry of Shipping, the petitioner was admitted in Sarkari Karmachari Hospital in Phulbaria, Dhaka on 19.1.89. The certificate of the petitioner's admission and release from hospital is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure 'F'. The petitioner claims that he submitted all the aforesaid copies of annexures along with his application dated 18.2.89 Annexure 'G' mentioning therein the dates of his earlier application of leave and sought further medical leave from 22.1.89 to 7.3.89 as per advice of the hospital's doctor which is annexed and marked as Annexure 'H'. Thereafter on the same medical ground as per advice of the hospital doctor he filed two applications for medical leave from 8.3.89 to 28.3.89 and from 29.3.89 to 30.4.89 which are annexed to the petition and marked as Annexures 'I' and 'J'. The petitioner claims that without prior notice of show cause he was dismissed from service on 15.4.89 vide office Memo No. 240/89 marked as Annexure 'K' due to alleged absence from duty without authorised leave in violation of BIWTA service rule enumerated in sections 6(iii), 7, 8, 9 10 and 11 of Discipline and Appeal Regulations 1984. It is further stated that no enquiry was held and the petitioner was deprived of the opportunity to be heard in person by the competent authority before inflicting major or minor penalties as per section 5(2) of the service rules. 

 25. Now we are to see whether he was absent in accordance with the Discipline and Appeal Regulation, 1984. Note (i) to the Regulation No. 6 of the Discipline and Appeal Regulations, 1984 states that an employee should normally obtain prior permission and sanction of leave before he absents himself from duty. Note (ii) states that if for some reasons, it is not possible for him to comply with the provisions of note (i), he should ensure that his application for leave should reach his controlling officer within the specific period of thirty days along with reasons for not obtaining prior sanction of leave. We find from the leave application that the petitioner had not applied for prior sanction of leave nor he has ever given any reason in his application for not obtaining prior sanction of leave. Therefore these applications for leave were not made in accordance with the Discipline and Appeal Regulations, 1984 which was framed in exercise of the power conferred by section 3 of Inland Transport Authority Ordinance, 1958 (East Pakistan Ordinance No. LXXV of 1958) read with rule of the Inland Water Authority Rules, 1959. There is no paper to show that BIWTA had sanctioned leave to the petitioner for his alleged illness. 

 30. He has relied on (b) above where the Supreme Court has held that if the service of the petitioner is terminated in violation of principle of natural justice the employee has a similar right of action as in (a) This decision however does not cover the situation where an employee is removed under statutory rules which excludes holding of inquiry in certain circumstance. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman appearing for the respondents has submitted that the principle of natural justice is not applicable where there is a positive legislation dispensing with such observance. In this connection he has cited the case of Md. Sekander Hossain Vs. Secretary, Ministry of Cabinet Affairs Establishment Division, Government of Bangladesh and others reported in 29 DLR 10 where it was held by this court;
